leads.question: Map the 4 TLOAD, 14 SSTORE and 23 SLOAD sites left unrun by theme-monad-gcc-terminators to source lines with opcodes/jumpmap.json and cycles/012/theme-bytecode-coverage.work/srcmap.py. For those that compile src/libraries/CurrencyDelta.sol:21-39, src/libraries/NonzeroDeltaCount.sol:14-32, src/libraries/Lock.sol:25 or src/libraries/CurrencyReserves.sol:17-36, run the body of compile_basic_blocks<MonadTraits<r>> for MONAD_TEN on the logged cycle 31 states in the model and compare the key, the value and the spill registers around each runtime call with the clang listing. Does any emitted TLOAD or SSTORE use a stale stack element for its slot or value?
leads.why: These are the last emitter classes on the PoolManager's un-entered blocks that no one has run from the shipped package, on the only network where validators execute native code that eth_call never runs. A TLOAD that read the wrong slot in the delta or count path would let unlock pass src/PoolManager.sol:111 with an open debit, which is an unprivileged siphon of every pool.

leads.question: The verifier of theme-closed-producer-operand-census cleared the MULMOD sites at pc 22585, 22639 and 23094 (src/libraries/SqrtPriceMath.sol:250-252) by saying a product of 2^256 or more makes amount1 at least 2^160, which no realistic token supply reaches. computeSwapStep computes getAmount1Delta to the step target before it compares the result with the amount left (src/libraries/SwapMath.sol:68-69 and :89-91), so the amount is never transferred. Over the live pools on MegaETH and Monad, what is the largest liquidity times (sqrtPriceTarget - sqrtPriceCurrent) a swap with a far price limit can reach in one step, given the word boundary that TickBitmap.nextInitializedTickWithinOneWord imposes for each tick spacing? Does any pool of ordinary tokens reach 2^256?
leads.why: If it does, the clearance rests on a wrong premise and those pcs are reachable by any swapper in ordinary pools. A wrong remainder or quotient there would flip the comparison at SwapMath.sol:69 and let a swap reach the target price for a wrong input amount. The class itself was executed elsewhere on MegaETH, so the expected answer is a corrected premise, not a fault.

leads.question: OPCODES.md lists the cache keys of the prewarm cache in each reth-derived release as unread. In reth v2.11.0, the execution cache (crate reth_execution_cache, used by crates/engine/tree/src/tree/payload_processor/mod.rs:446-509 and saved by prewarm.rs:468-499 through insert_state) is keyed by parent hash. When a block creates a contract, writes its storage and destroys it in the same transaction (EIP-6780), and a later block recreates code at the same address, does insert_state drop the cached storage of the destroyed account, so that the new account reads zero? And does the BAL prefetch at payload_processor/mod.rs:410 insert values read from the parent state or values the block access list declares?
leads.why: A stale cached slot would make one node read a storage word that differs from the state, inside a PoolManager call or a token's balanceOf at src/types/Currency.sol:94. On a single sequencer network the sequencer's reading becomes the block. The first part needs only an ordinary account that deploys and destroys its own contract.
